outcome: Maternal outcomes (Preeclampsia, Gestational Diabetes Mellitus, Polyhydramnios, Oligohydramnios with Intrauterine Growth Retardation)
Perinatal outcomes (Live births, Stillbirth, Intrauterine Fetal Demise, Early Neonatal death, Newborn APGAR Score)
Mode of delivery (Normal Vaginal Delivery, Caesarean Section)
cohort: The study included 60 women with Rh Negative pregnancy, predominantly aged 21-25 years, with O Negative being the most common blood group, conducted at ACSR Government General Hospital, Nellore, Andhra Pradesh, India.
finding: The study found a 2.36% prevalence of Rh Negative pregnancy with generally favorable perinatal outcomes, including 96.6% live births and 78.3% of newborns having an APGAR score of 10, though antenatal prophylaxis uptake was suboptimal at 40%.
mod_finding: 70% of mothers had Normal Vaginal Deliveries while 25% underwent Caesarean Section.
